Outer (envelope) surface of a cortical surface

Source: R/mris-outer-surface.R
mris_outer_surface.Rd

Computes the smooth surface that wraps a pial surface without dipping into the sulci: the surface FreeSurfer writes as ?h.pial-outer-smoothed when it computes the local gyrification index (mris_compute_lgi, run by recon-all -localGI), re-implemented here without 'MATLAB'.

The envelope is not a convex hull. It is a morphological closing of the volume inside the pial surface: a dilation followed by an erosion with a disk or ball of radius close_radius, which fills every gap the element cannot enter. The sulci, which are narrower than the element, are bridged, while concavities broader than the element are followed. A convex hull is the limit of an infinitely large element.

Usage

mris_outer_surface(
  surface,
  close_radius = 15,
  smooth_iterations = 30L,
  method = c("freesurfer", "isotropic"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

surface

pial surface of one hemisphere, in FreeSurfer surface (tkrRAS) coordinates, for example read with freesurferformats::read.fs.surface; see ensure_mesh3d for the accepted classes. The surface must be closed, but it does not need to be free of topological defects

close_radius

radius of the closing element in millimeters; default is 15, the --close_sphere_size default of mris_compute_lgi. That script documents the value as the sphere diameter, but its code uses it as the radius; pass 7.5 for a 15-millimeter diameter. A value of 0 skips the closing

smooth_iterations

number of neighbor-averaging rounds applied to the extracted surface; default is 30, the --smooth_iters default of mris_compute_lgi

method

"freesurfer" (default) to reproduce the FreeSurfer output, or "isotropic" for a three-dimensional closing; see 'Details'

verbose

whether to print progress messages; default is FALSE

Value

A triangular mesh of class 'mesh3d' (with vb, it, and normals) in the coordinates of surface. Its attribute "info" is a named list with method, close_radius, smooth_iterations, delta (the shift of the inside test, in millimeters), grid_origin and grid_dim (the corner coordinates and dimension of the working lattice), odd_columns (lattice columns that crossed surface an odd number of times and were left empty; non-zero for open or self-intersecting input), n_components (connected components of the extracted surface before the largest one is kept), is_closed_manifold (see vcg_count_edge_defects), and euler (the Euler characteristic of the result; 2 for a closed surface without handles).

Details

With method = "freesurfer" (default), the steps reproduce mris_compute_lgi as it is coded:

  1. Fill the lattice points that lie inside surface, as mris_fill -c -r 1 does. The lattice is 1 millimeter apart and aligned with integer surface coordinates (the conformed volume). The inside test is evaluated at the lattice points shifted by delta (less than half a millimeter per axis): mris_fill fills a grid anchored at the smallest vertex coordinate and then re-samples it onto the conformed grid with nearest-neighbor interpolation.

  2. Grow the filled volume by one voxel toward the right (+x) and superior (+z) sides only. This is what the "soft Gaussian filter" of make_outer_surface.m (a 2-by-2 kernel followed by a threshold) amounts to.

  3. Close the volume with a disk of radius close_radius millimeters, independently in every coronal slice. The structuring element strel('ball', 15, 15) in make_outer_surface.m is two-dimensional, so nothing is bridged along the anterior-posterior axis.

  4. Extract the surface of the closed 0/255 volume with marching cubes at level 100, as isosurface does in make_outer_surface.m.

  5. Keep the largest connected component, as mris_extract_main_component does.

  6. Apply smooth_iterations rounds of include-self neighbor averaging, as mris_smooth -nw -n 30 does (see mris_smooth).

On both hemispheres of the N27 template, every vertex of the surfaces FreeSurfer generated lies within 0.9 millimeters of the result (mean nearest-vertex distance 0.34 millimeters).

With method = "isotropic", the volume is closed with a three-dimensional ball of radius close_radius instead, with no one-sided growth, no delta shift, and marching cubes at (just below) the midpoint level. This is the procedure the FreeSurfer documentation describes. The result does not depend on how the head is oriented in the volume, but it differs from the FreeSurfer output by up to a few millimeters.

References

A surface-based approach to quantify local cortical gyrification. IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, 27(2), 161-170 (2008).

See also

mris_smooth, fill_surface

Examples


# Two boxes 4 millimeters apart: the envelope bridges the gap
volume <- array(0, c(64, 40, 40))
volume[10:28, 10:30, 10:30] <- 1
volume[33:51, 10:30, 10:30] <- 1
boxes <- vcg_isosurface(volume, threshold_lb = 0.5, vox_to_ras = diag(4))

envelope <- mris_outer_surface(boxes, close_radius = 8)
attr(envelope, "info")$n_components
#> [1] 1

plot_mesh_polygon(
  list(boxes, envelope),
  alpha = c(1, 0.3),
  col = list("gray", "red"),
  main = "Gray: input; red: outer surface"
)
